title: AOA Trace File
description: A trace file is a JSON object with an optional `version` and a `spans` array. Spans are ordered by a monotonically non-decreasing `seq` key.

version.description: Wire-format version of the trace envelope. Absent is treated as version 1 for backward compatibility; a reader rejects a version it does not support.

type.description: The kind of span. One of the eleven stable discriminants. Only write.committed attests a mutation that landed; write.attempt is intent recorded before execution, and write.failed/write.denied/write.blocked all mean the write did not land.

seq.description: Monotonic ordering key within the trace.

attributes.description: Free-form span-type-specific metadata. Keys named here carry a published meaning that readers depend on; any other key is unconstrained.

results.description: The artifacts a retrieval span ranked, best first. Absent and empty are DIFFERENT observations and readers must not collapse them: absent means the trace carries no retrieval-ranking instrumentation at all (no evidence, so Recall@k and MRR are unavailable), while an empty array means a retriever ran and ranked nothing (a measured zero, so Recall@k is 0.0). A producer that cannot report a ranking must omit the key rather than emit an empty array.
